title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
summary: The roadmap facts and Message Center rollout window are accurately reported. Hold because the licensing field and preparation advice imply a confirmed licensing route for the group report while the body correctly says its licensing is unpublished; the general reporting row also incorrectly labels automation as undocumented. Microsoft's two PowerShell pages disagree about the user-input parameter, which needs an explicit caveat.

claims.claim: An automation counterpart for accessing the existing Data access governance reports is not documented.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center.

This cmdlet fetches details of various DAG reports available in SharePoint admin center.
claims.fix: Replace this generic reporting row's null API with Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity>, linking its reference page. Note that it lists existing reports and does not establish support for the new arbitrary-group report; alternatively remove this redundant generic row.

claims.claim: The user report is reached through Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users > View reports > Create report.
claims.quote:
From the Data access governance landing page, select **View reports** under **Site permissions for users**.
2. Select **Create report** to generate your report.

claims.claim: The cited PowerShell guide documents Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight with PermissionsReport, Snapshot, SharePoint, Name and UserEmailList for the user report.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name "UserSharePointReport" -UserEmailList "a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"
claims.fix: Explicitly report the documentation disagreement: the cited guide uses -UserEmailList, but https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/start-spodataaccessgovernanceinsight?view=sharepoint-ps lists -UserPrincipalNames as mandatory in UserPermissionsParameterSet and does not list -UserEmailList. Prefer the reference spelling in the copyable command and cite both pages; do not imply the guide's spelling is independently confirmed by the reference.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide site permissions report must have been generated at least once before generating the user report.
claims.quote: Make sure that the site permissions for your organization report is generated at least once.

claims.claim: The group report's default state is not stated, represented by unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance group permissions report licensing price meter default enabled role; SharePoint group permissions report default on enable licensing billing meter price. Read roadmap, MC1540348, DAG overview and SAM prerequisites; none states this control's default.

claims.claim: The briefing assigns the group report a confirmed mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: model: "mixed"; notes: "Licensing for the group report itself is not yet published."; Open questions: "Which licence and role does the group report need"

claims.claim: Group-based access accounts for most oversharing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint oversharing most group based access site permissions groups. Read DAG overview and returned excerpts for organisation permissions, special groups and modern sharing permissions; none says group-based access accounts for most oversharing.
claims.fix: Replace "Group-based access is how most oversharing happens quietly" with "Broad-membership groups can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients", which the roadmap and MC1540348 state. Present the site-by-site comparison as analysis rather than an absolute claim about what reviews can never show.

claims.where: Why it matters: group membership and access
claims.claim: Granting a SharePoint group permissions grants those group permissions to its members.
claims.quote: All the users in a group automatically have the permission level of the group.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/default-sharepoint-groups to sources for the group-permission inheritance premise.

claims.claim: The Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight reference has no ReportEntity value for reporting on an arbitrary specified group.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance report given group permissions report PowerShell group ReportEntity. Read the complete Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight syntax and ReportEntity values; PermissionsReport and PermissionedUsers are listed, but no arbitrary-group selector.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The notice describes administrator reporting and does not announce automatic changes to group permissions or member-facing behaviour.
claims.quote: SharePoint administrators will be able to use the new report to identify all sites accessible to a given group. The report will show the extent of the group's access to those sites.

claims.claim: The checklist names controls that are missing from the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Check the Reports setting"; "Run the site permissions for your organisation report first"; "Restricted access control or Site access review". Table rows cover only the group report, general DAG access and the user report.
claims.fix: Add rows for the Microsoft 365 Reports concealment setting, the organisation-wide permissions baseline, Restricted access control and Site access review, reading their exact paths and automation before filling them. Alternatively remove optional remediation instructions from the checklist and keep them as background notes.
